reason: The villus is the absorption site, and glucose is one of the nutrients the first goal asks us to send toward the liver.
expectation: Glucose should cross the intestinal lining into a blood vessel, potentially alongside amino acids.

effect: Glucose crossed into a villus blood capillary; amino acids still need to cross.
reaction: The result matched the expected blood route.
reason: Amino acids are the other nutrient the goal asks to send toward the liver, and the villus is their absorption site.
expectation: Amino acids will cross the intestinal lining into villus blood.

effect: Amino acids also crossed into villus blood; both nutrients are now ready for their onward route.
reaction: That matched the expected absorption route.
reason: The fat products need to cross the villus and be packaged for their different route.
expectation: The intestinal cell will take up the fat products and may use the available packaging materials.

effect: Fat digestion products entered intestinal cells but have not yet been packaged.
reaction: The uptake was as expected; packaging remains a separate step.
reason: The available packaging materials should prepare the absorbed fat for its lymph route.
expectation: The intestinal cells will package the fat into lipoprotein particles.

effect: Packaging required the villus as a hotspot; the automatic reaction produced chylomicrons inside intestinal cells.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the station-based step.
reason: Chylomicrons need to enter the villus's central lymph vessel, whose entrance is available.
expectation: The packaged fat will enter the lacteal and travel into lymph.

effect: Chylomicrons entered lymph through the villus, completing the fat-transport goal; glucose and amino acids still need an onward route.
reaction: The villus was again required as the station, which makes the earlier packaging feedback useful.
reason: The remaining liver route is not visible among the initial items, so checking the glucose's available partners should clarify the next step.
expectation: The inspection should reveal how the absorbed glucose can proceed toward the liver.

effect: The inspection automatically combined the two absorbed nutrients into portal blood, completing the liver-route goal and the chapter.
reaction: The automatic combination was a useful resolution, though the portal route became clear only at the end.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following fat into intestinal cells, packaging it into chylomicrons and sending it into lymph made its different route from glucose and amino acids concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate glucose and amino-acid absorption steps had nearly identical picture descriptions, making that passage somewhat repetitive.

surprise.text: Packaging and lymph entry both required the villus hotspot rather than directly combining the visibly relevant ingredients; compatibility feedback completed each operation automatically.

arbitrary.text: The need to select the villus for packaging and lacteal entry was not obvious from the ingredient titles, even though the feedback made the required operation clear.

continue.text: I would continue: contrasting blood and lymph routes was a useful construction, although I would want clearer explanations of terms such as portal blood and lacteal for the intended audience.
